name: Scrapgospel Burned-Scripture Patchwork Coat
description:
A floor-length coat assembled entirely from salvage: defunct transit upholstery, acid-bleached denim, torn synthetic prayer flags, and heat-fused industrial tarp panels. Worn by adherents of the Scrapgospel movement — a Shelf-born spiritual tradition that holds material reclamation as sacred act. Each panel is hand-painted with fragments of the Scrapgospel liturgy in Tagalog-Igbo creole script, using rust-water ink and carbon-black pigment.

No two coats share the same scripture arrangement; construction is considered a devotional practice. Hems are deliberately unfinished and fraying — entropy is doctrine. Acid-rain staining is accepted and incorporated as evidence of endurance. Worn open over whatever else the wearer has.
functionality: Heavy layered construction provides wind and light-rain protection. Deep interior pockets sewn from scrap. Gene-compatible — open construction accommodates tails, wings, or spinal geneware without modification.
what_it_says: I have made something sacred from what the city threw away, and I will not be erased.
story_hooks: A specific coat is rumored to contain panels cut from the original Scrapgospel founder's vestments — and someone upstack wants to buy it.
A Tier 4 fashion house debuts a 'deconstructed liturgical' collection clearly derived from Scrapgospel aesthetics; the community is deciding how to respond.
The scripture on one coat, when photographed and assembled, reveals a map of something hidden beneath the Shelf.

physical_description.visual_profile: A dramatic, floor-length ceremonial coat that reads as lived-in sacred garment rather than fashion. Silhouette is deliberately shapeless and flowing, constructed from visibly mismatched fabric panels in competing textures and fades. The coat hangs open, revealing layers beneath, with an almost liturgical weight despite its construction from refuse. Overall impression is spiritual ascetic meets environmental salvage artist.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized and unstructured; designed to drape loosely from shoulders to floor without conforming to the body. Armholes are generously cut for layering. No tailoring — the fit is accidental, determined by how panels were assembled.
physical_description.primary_material: Mixed salvage composite: defunct transit upholstery (vinyl and wool blend), acid-bleached and distressed denim, synthetic prayer flag material (nylon), heat-fused industrial tarp (PVC-treated polymer), all hand-joined with visible stitching or fusion seams.
physical_description.texture: Highly varied tactile landscape — smooth cracked vinyl adjacent to rough denim, brittle synthetic flagging material, stiff industrial tarp sections. Hand-painted surfaces are matte with visible brush marks and pigment granulation. Intentional surface deterioration creates ridged, flaking areas.
physical_description.color_scheme: Desaturated and acid-damaged palette: bleached indigo, rust-brown oxidation stains, charcoal hand-painted text, cream acid-rain spotting, olive tarp green, faded burgundy upholstery. All colors appear sun-faded and chemically altered. Accent colors emerge from rust-water ink (deep orange-brown) and carbon-black liturgical text.
physical_description.closures: None — coat is worn entirely open. Some panels show evidence of previous fasteners (ghost button holes, magnetic snap failures) that are left unfastened or deliberately disconnected as part of the aesthetic.
distinctive_features: Hand-painted Tagalog-Igbo creole script covering most surface area — unique scripture arrangement on each coat
Deliberately fraying hemline, unfinished and raw throughout
Visible heat-fusion seams where tarp panels overlap denim
Acid-rain staining patterns incorporated as intentional design element
Layered patchwork construction where seams are visible and emphasized
Synthetic prayer flag fragments still attached to interior or edges
Evidence of previous garment hardware (zippers, snaps) left non-functional
Carbon-black pigment flaking and cracking across text areas
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade / ungoverned. Scrapgospel is a Shelf-born movement — the coat signals voluntary material austerity and spiritual rejection of consumer culture, not poverty.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Scrapgospel adherents as explicit spiritual marker and act of faith. The wearer is signaling: radical environmentalism, Shelf-born identity, material reclamation as sacred practice, rejection of corporate fashion systems, deep community rootedness. This is countercultural and intentional, not desperate.
physical_description.condition_typical: Perpetually weathered and in active deterioration. Fraying accelerates with wear. Paint flakes with movement. Stains accumulate and are welcomed. The coat is never 'finished' — it is always in process, always receiving new marks from the world.
